question: What is irritability (感應性) in living organisms?
options: The ability to synthesize organic food from inorganic substances
The ability to detect changes (stimuli) in the internal or external environment and produce appropriate responses
The permanent increase in dry mass and cell number over time
The removal of metabolic waste products from the body

question: Which structure in the human eye is transparent, curved, and responsible for most of the refraction (bending) of light rays entering the eye?
options: Iris / 虹膜
Cornea / 角膜
Retina / 視網膜
Sclera / 鞏膜

question: The choroid (脈絡膜) contains black pigment that absorbs excess light inside the eyeball to prevent internal reflection, and has a rich network of blood capillaries to supply oxygen and nutrients to the retina.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How does the iris regulate the amount of light entering the eye when a person walks from a dark room into bright sunlight?
options: Circular muscles of the iris contract and radial muscles relax, constricting the pupil
Radial muscles of the iris contract and circular muscles relax, dilating the pupil
Both circular and radial muscles relax, keeping the pupil size constant
Ciliary muscles contract to pull the iris over the pupil

question: Which combination of changes occurs during eye accommodation (視覺調節) when focusing on a nearby object?
options: Ciliary muscles relax → suspensory ligaments become taut → lens becomes thinner (less convex)
Ciliary muscles contract → suspensory ligaments slacken → lens becomes thicker (more convex)
Ciliary muscles contract → suspensory ligaments become taut → lens becomes thinner (less convex)
Ciliary muscles relax → suspensory ligaments slacken → lens becomes thicker (more convex)

question: When viewing a distant object, light rays reaching the eye are nearly parallel and require less refraction, so the lens becomes thinner (less convex).
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Why is there no image perceived when light falls on the blind spot (盲點) of the retina?
options: It is covered by a thick opaque layer of melanin.
It is the region where optic nerve fibres leave the eyeball and contains no photoreceptor cells (rods or cones).
It contains only rod cells, which do not function in daylight.
The lens cannot focus light onto the blind spot.

question: Which comparison between rod cells (視桿細胞) and cone cells (視錐細胞) in the human retina is CORRECT?
options: Rods are concentrated at the yellow spot (fovea) and provide high visual acuity, whereas cones are scattered across the periphery.
Rods are highly sensitive to dim light and provide black-and-white vision, whereas cones require bright light and provide colour vision.
Rods detect red, green, and blue wavelengths, whereas cones contain visual purple (rhodopsin).
Multiple cone cells share a single optic nerve fibre, whereas each rod cell connects to its own individual neurone.

question: The yellow spot (fovea / 黃點) contains a very high density of cone cells and no rod cells, giving the sharpest and most detailed colour vision when looking directly at an object.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: What causes short-sightedness (myopia / 近視), and which type of lens is used to correct it?
options: The eyeball is too short or the lens is too thin; corrected with a convex lens
The eyeball is too long or the lens is too thick (too convex), focusing images of distant objects in front of the retina; corrected with a concave (diverging) lens
Uneven curvature of the cornea; corrected with a cylindrical lens
Loss of elasticity of the lens due to old age; corrected with a concave lens

question: In long-sightedness (hypermetropia / 遠視), where are light rays from a nearby object focused, and what lens corrects this defect?
options: Focused behind the retina; corrected with a convex (converging) lens
Focused in front of the retina; corrected with a concave (diverging) lens
Focused directly on the blind spot; corrected with a prism
Scattered across the vitreous humour; corrected with a flat glass lens

question: Red-green colour blindness (紅綠色盲) is a hereditary condition caused by the absence or defect of one or more types of cone cells in the retina.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which structure in the human middle ear equalizes air pressure on both sides of the eardrum (tympanic membrane / 鼓膜)?
options: Cochlea / 耳蝸
Semicircular canals / 半規管
Eustachian tube / 耳咽管
Oval window / 卵圓窗

question: What is the function of the three ear ossicles (malleus, incus, and stapes / 聽小骨) in the middle ear?
options: To secrete earwax that traps dust particles
To transmit and amplify vibrations from the eardrum to the oval window of the inner ear
To convert nerve impulses into sound waves
To detect rotational movements of the head

question: Sensory hair cells inside the cochlea (耳蝸) detect pressure vibrations in the cochlear fluid and generate nerve impulses that travel along the auditory nerve to the brain.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which structures in the human inner ear detect the position and movement of the head to help maintain body balance?
options: Cochlea and round window
Semicircular canals (半規管) and vestibule (utricle and saccule)
Pinna and auditory canal
Eardrum and Eustachian tube

question: What is phototropism (向光性) in flowering plants?
options: The rapid folding of leaflets when touched
The directional growth movement of a plant part in response to unilateral light
The opening and closing of stomata in response to humidity
The growth of roots towards mineral fertilizers

question: Plant shoots generally exhibit positive phototropism (growing towards light) and negative gravitropism (growing upwards away from gravity), which positions leaves to receive maximum sunlight for photosynthesis.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: In classic coleoptile (胚芽鞘) experiments, what happens when a mica plate (impermeable to chemicals) is inserted horizontally just below the tip on the shaded side, and the coleoptile is illuminated from one side?
options: The coleoptile bends strongly towards the light source.
The coleoptile fails to bend towards the light because the mica plate blocks the downward transport of auxins (生長素) on the shaded side.
The coleoptile bends away from the light source.
The tip dies immediately.

question: How does unilateral light cause a plant shoot to bend towards the light source?
options: Light destroys all auxins on both sides of the shoot.
Auxins migrate from the illuminated side to the shaded side; the higher auxin concentration on the shaded side stimulates faster cell elongation than on the illuminated side.
Auxins accumulate on the illuminated side and inhibit cell division.
Cells on the shaded side undergo rapid meiosis.

question: Unlike shoots, high concentrations of auxins INHIBIT cell elongation in roots, causing a horizontally placed root to bend downwards (positive gravitropism / 正向地性).
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: When a potted plant is placed horizontally on a rotating clinostat (旋轉器) in darkness, how does its shoot grow?
options: It bends sharply upwards.
It bends sharply downwards.
It grows straight horizontally because slow rotation distributes gravity and auxins evenly on all sides.
It stops growing completely.

question: In plants, auxins are produced at the apical meristems of shoot tips and root tips and move away from the tips mainly by diffusion and active transport.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤
